_note: Placeholder vocabulary for milestone 1. Names and flavour are drafts for Lys to overwrite. Nothing here is code; changing a name is a JSON edit.
_namingNote: Where a thing has a commonly-used te reo Māori name in Aotearoa, that is its name here — not the English one. pāua, heru, maro and pounamu are all already the ordinary word for the thing; "green stone" was the outlier and is now pounamu. Biome follows the real thing too: pounamu comes out of West Coast rivers and off beaches, not out of forest floor, so it sits in beach. It swapped places with the humming geode rather than simply moving, because resolveItem() picks uniformly among the items matching a tier+biome and leaving forest tier 4 with a single entry would have made every forest Wonder the same feather.
_tier6Note: Lyss splits the top of the ladder by FUNCTION, not rarity. An Epic find is 'just from another world' — a sci-fi heru, a chainmail maro. An Epic epic find 'grants you supernatural ability'. Tier 6 is therefore never rolled and never scattered: biome 'granted' matches no chunk, so the only way one exists is for a cryptid to hand it to you. That path is not built yet. The data is here so the ladder is real, and so the escalated Epic sequence has something to escalate FOR.
_elsewhereWeightsNote: Where the good stuff is: Wonders at 22 against the forest's 6. Tier 5 is NOT on this table, same as at home; elsewhere's Epics are hand-placed by worldgen/elsewhere.js and pinned, so the scheduler's promise (never on a weight table) holds in both worlds. The offer book reads this table for any object carrying biome 'elsewhere'.

_authoredNote: biome 'authored' matches no chunk biome and no weight table, like 'granted'. These are the cryptid finds: tier 5, hand-placed within cryptidArea.radius of a site by src/worldgen/cryptids.js, pinned with offers.force, never scattered. No body parts of any cryptid as items — no hair, no scale-of-a-body, no bone, no tooth. 'a scale that isn't' is allowed only because it says it is not one.
_tier6FlavourNote: tier-6 flavour is OBSERVATION: what it is like to hold, never who made it or what the cryptid is. Lyss's memo says an Epic epic 'grants you supernatural ability', and the first drafts promised one each — knowing the way out, carrying more — but no such mechanic exists in the game, and a player who reads 'you are sure which way is out' will test it on the spot in elsewhere. When an ability is built, its flavour can say so; until then these are placeholders that describe the thing and promise nothing.
_epicExamplesNote: Both of Lyss's own Epic-find examples are now in: 'a scifi fucking heru' and 'a chainmail maro'. The maro was unresolved through milestone 4 because three transcription passes of her voice memo gave three different words; Juniper confirmed it from the memos on 2026-08-28.
_grantedNote: biome 'granted' deliberately matches no chunk biome, so tier 6 can never be scattered into the world. See _tier6Note.
_nearNote: An optional `near` field says an item wants a particular kind of ground. `near: "water"` means the beach OR a creek bed — which is where pounamu actually comes from: West Coast rivers and the beaches below them, not the forest floor. Now that the world has streams, a forest point within a few metres of one counts as a riverbed and pounamu can turn up in it. Items without `near` are unaffected and appear anywhere their biome allows.
